title: पाश्चात्य भाषिक चिन्तन परम्परामा ग्राइसको  संवाद र सहयोग सिद्धान्त
nepali: पाउल ग्राइसको संवादात्मक सहयोग सिद्धान्त पाश्चात्य भाषिक चिन्तकहरूका निरन्तर चिन्तन परम्पराको एक महत्त्वपूर्ण उपलब्धी हो । यो सिद्धान्त ग्राइसले हार्वड विश्वविद्यालयमा दिएका व्याख्यानहरूमा आधारित छ । उनका व्याख्यानको सारस्वरूप यो १९७५ मा प्रकाशित Logic and Conversation वा तर्क र संवाद शीर्षकको लेखमा समेटिएको छ । ग्राइसले संवादलाई अर्थपूर्ण, उद्देश्यपूर्ण र सहज बनाउन, संवादको गुणस्तर, संवादको मात्रा, संवादमा अन्तरसम्बन्ध तथा संवादको तरिका (गुणोक्ति, परिमाणोक्ति, सम्बन्धोक्ति र व्यवहारोक्ति) जस्ता चार सूत्रहरू अघि सारे । यी चारवटा सूत्रको प्रयोग गर्दै संवादका सिलसिलामा वक्ताले असत्य र प्रमाणहीन कुरा बोल्नु हुँदैन, सत्य र ठरिहने कुरा बोलेर संवादलाई गुणस्तरीय बनाउनु पर्छ । असावधानी साथ गलत भएको रहेछ भने गल्ती सच्याउने आचारसंहिता पालन गर्नुपर्छ भन्ने सल्लाह दिइएका छन् । यसैगरी चाहिने कुरा बोल्नु र नचाहिने कुरा नबोल्नु भन्ने उनको परिमाणोक्ति सूत्रको अन्तर्यय हो । संवादलाई लक्ष्योन्मुख र उपलब्धीपूर्ण बनाउन प्रश्न र उत्तरको प्रसङ्ग वा धारा पनि मिल्नु पर्छ । यसको संवादलाई बलियो बनाउँछ । सम्बन्ध बलियो भयो भने संवादको सन्दर्भ र सिलसिला मिल्छ भन्ने सम्बन्धोक्तिको मर्म हो । भन्न खोजेको कुरा नढाँटी नअल्मलिई सावधानीसाथ सुरैले भन्नुपर्छ । तरिका नमिलाई गरिएको संवाद अर्थहीन बन्न जाने भएकाले अभिव्यक्तिमा अस्पष्टता र आशंका हटाएर सङ्क्षेपमा र क्रमैसँग भन्नुपर्छ भन्ने व्यवहारोक्तिको आसय हो । यसरी संवादलाई सहज, स्पष्ट, प्रभावकारी बनाउन र भाषालाई मानवीय विचार, भाव तथा धारणा आदानप्रदानको प्रभावकारी साधनका रूपमा प्रयोग गर्नका लागि ग्राइसको संवादात्मक सहयोग सिद्धान्त एक महŒवपूर्ण मार्गदर्शन रहेको छ । प्रस्तुत अध्ययनमा भाषाको सामान्य परिचय, भाषाका कार्य, भाषासम्बन्धी चिन्तनका पाश्चात्य मत तथा परम्पराको चर्चा गर्दै उपलब्ध स्रोतमा केन्द्रित भई ग्राइसका भाषिक चिन्तन र योगदानको चर्चा पुस्तकीय अध्ययन कार्यका आधारमा विश्लेषणात्मक पद्धति अपनाइएर गरिएको छ ।
american_english: Paul Grice's conversational cooperative principle is an important achievement of the continuous tradition of thought among Western linguistic thinkers. This principle is based on the lectures delivered by Grice at Harvard University. As the essence of his lectures, it is encompassed in the article titled Logic and Conversation, or Tark ra Samvad, published in 1975. In order to make conversation meaningful, purposeful, and smooth, Grice put forward four maxims, namely conversational quality, conversational quantity, conversational relation, and conversational manner (maxims of quality, quantity, relation, and manner). Applying these four maxims, in the course of conversation a speaker must not state false and unsubstantiated things, but must make the conversation qualitative by speaking what is true and verifiable. Advice is given that if an error has occurred inadvertently, one must adhere to a code of conduct for correcting mistakes. Likewise, speaking what is necessary and not speaking what is unnecessary is the core of his maxim of quantity. In order to make conversation goal-oriented and fruitful, the context or flow of question and answer must also correspond. This strengthens conversation. The essence of the maxim of relation is that if the connection is strong, the context and coherence of the conversation will align. What one intends to say should be stated without deception, without wavering, carefully, and straightforwardly. Because conversation conducted without proper manner turns out to be meaningless, the intent of the maxim of manner is that one must speak concisely and orderly, removing ambiguity and doubt from expression. In this way, Grice's conversational cooperative principle remains an important guide for making conversation smooth, clear, and effective, and for using language as an effective instrument for exchanging human thoughts, feelings, and ideas. In the present study, discussing the general introduction to language, functions of language, and Western views and traditions of linguistic thought, and focusing on available sources, a discussion of Grice's linguistic thought and contribution is carried out based on desk research adopting an analytical method.

In order to make conversation meaningful, purposeful and smooth, Grice put forward four maxims: conversational quality, conversational quantity, conversational relation and conversational manner (maxims of quality, quantity, relation and manner). Advice is given that if an error has occurred inadvertently, one ought to abide by a code of conduct for correcting mistakes. In like manner, speaking what is necessary and not speaking what is unnecessary is the substance of his maxim of quantity. In order to make conversation goal-oriented and fruitful, the context or flow of question and answer must also harmonise. This fortifies conversation. The crux of the maxim of relation is that if the relationship is strong, the context and coherence of the conversation will fall into line. What one intends to say ought to be said without dissembling, without faltering, carefully and directly. Because conversation conducted without an appropriate manner becomes meaningless, the intention of the maxim of manner is that one must speak concisely and in due order, eliminating ambiguity and uncertainty from expression. In the present study, discussing the general introduction to language, functions of language, and Western opinions and traditions of linguistic thought, and concentrating on available sources, a discussion of Grice's linguistic thought and contribution is conducted on the basis of documentary research adopting an analytical method.
